items.name: First screen
items.reason: Headline, flag and decision block alone say what to do (ship Brisk-S low reasoning with one retry, J), why (the only one of eighteen inside both gates; five reach 97%, ten stay under 600 ms, checked against options_dominance), and the main risk (clears 97% by 0.1 points, interval 96.2% to 98.1%, a run of today's size reads it below the line 38.6% of the time). c1's gate scatter shows the single survivor at a glance.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: c1 (only survivor) -> c2 (its clearance is noise) -> c3 (every safer option misses latency) -> c4 (one retry is what lifts it) -> c5 (where headroom might come from) feeds the next slot and next steps directly. Headline, lede, watch and explore 3 agree. The c2 caption's 'only the pick's interval crosses the line' contradicts its own block (row E), but that is a wording error, not a break in the argument.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The pick's weak axis is stated on the first screen and repeated in c2, watch and the confidence caveats; c4 says the reasoning gain (+0.8, -0.4 to +2.1) is not separated, and next step 3 says L's case is margin, not a measured lead. Slight overreach: the confidence form 'high_if_immaterial' sits on a lead caveat that is close to a coin flip (38.6% wrong side, and best_of_n pushes it higher), and the lede states 38.6% without the 'if its true rate is today's' condition.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Most of the omissions check out: cost ranks one survivor; p95 budget sweep never changes the pick above 513 ms; off-reasoning and calls-per-task do not move the call. But the Nano-XS omission ('none is near the call') is not borne out by the pass-rate sweep: Nano-XS high reasoning with one retry (94.8%, 450 ms, $444 a month against the pick's $1,208) becomes the pick for any line from 92.7% to 94.8%, and is next in line after Brisk-S low no-retry. A reader weighing a relaxed pass line, which explore and next step 1 both invite, would want that option named.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: All four snapshot caveats (no_control, point_estimate:pass_rate, point_estimate:p95, best_of_n) are shown with material_if clauses. No control and unpaired effects are carried into c4 and Method; best_of_n is carried into watch and next step 2; missing task counts are carried into c5 and the omissions; p95 with no spread is stated. The unstated pass definition is in Method.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Three steps, each a declaration or an experiment with what it settles: declare point vs whole-interval reading (settles whether J passes today); re-run Brisk-S low with a second retry or a multi-hop fix on fresh cases watching the tail (settles whether a cheap option clears with its whole interval, and the best-of-eighteen luck); latency owner on 870 ms (settles whether L becomes the safer pick at $2,532 a month).

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: c1 gate_scatter, c4 diverging_bars and c5 bars plus examples fit their claims and the counterfactual holds. But c2's dot_interval caption says 'only the pick's interval crosses the line', and its own row E (Atlas-M high, no retry) reads 96.9% to 98.6%, which also crosses 97% (confirmed by spread.atlas-m.high.r0.pass_rate.overall.interval). c3's claim is about configurations whose interval clears the line (L, D, F), yet its range_bars include E, whose interval does not; the block shows latency but not which arms belong to the claimed set. The c2 settle table (16 columns, several dashes) carries one cited figure; its caption describes the one-sided need (38,350) while the watch slot cites the two-sided one (54,451).

findings.finding: Caption 'only the pick's interval crosses the line' is false on its own block: Atlas-M high reasoning, no retry (E) has an interval of 96.9% to 98.6%, which crosses 97%. Say 'the pick's interval crosses the line, and so does E's, which misses the latency budget', or drop E from the block.

Explore 'Pass-rate line': 'Lowered to 95.3% or below, Brisk-S low no-retry becomes the pick' is only true from 94.8% to 95.3%. The sweep (threshold:pass_rate) hands the pick to Nano-XS high reasoning with one retry from 92.7% to 94.8% ($444 a month), then to other Nano-XS settings lower down. State the band, and name the Nano-XS step, since it is a third of the pick's cost.

Omitted 'The Nano-XS configurations ... none is near the call' overstates. Nano-XS high with one retry is the next cheaper candidate once the pass line moves 2.2 points, and the omitted retry-by-model interaction (retry helps weaker models more) is the lever a 'buy headroom' experiment would pull. Either reword the reason or add Nano-XS high, one retry, to next step 2 as a cheaper headroom candidate.

The claim names configurations whose pass-rate interval clears the line (L, D, F), but the range_bars show J, L, D, E, F. Either restrict the block to L, D, F plus the pick or reword the claim to 'every configuration at or above the line'. Both are true, but the block and the claim should name the same set.

The lede and c2 state 'a fresh run of today's size would read the pick below the line 38.6% of the time' without the condition that the true rate equals today's. Under best_of_n the true rate likely reads lower, so 38.6% is the favourable case. Add the condition once on the first screen.

The watch slot cites the two-sided need (54,451 cases), while c2's settle table caption describes the one-sided need for the interval to sit wholly above the line (38,350). Cite the one the caption describes, or say why two-sided is the relevant reading. Both are impractical against 1,200 today, so the conclusion stands.

The confidence form 'high_if_immaterial' is generous when the lead caveat (point_estimate:pass_rate) has roughly a 39% chance of being material even before the best-of-eighteen correction. The material_if text is honest, but the form label reads stronger than the evidence.

invariant_concerns: Invariant 1 (minor): the c1 caption types a quantity, 'more than tenfold', with no figure key. It matches the block's own log-scale note, but it is a number in prose that does not resolve through a key.
Rendering text, not the report: the c2 settle table's note says 'Each bar is how often...' on a block that renders as a table, not bars.
